key_insight: Optimal control enables 12-ns CZ gates between tunable transmons with intrinsic errors near 2×10⁻⁵ while identifying operating regimes resilient to dephasing.
engineering_relevance: Smooth, single-shot flux pulses and noise-aware operating points offer a practical route to faster, more robust superconducting gates with less recalibration.
method: Optimize flux pulses while accounting for intrinsic Hamiltonian errors, energy relaxation, and dephasing.
Model fast electronics-induced dephasing and slow 1/f flux noise using published experimental measurements.
Identify dephasing sweet spots and exploit transmon asymmetry for noise resilience.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports 12-ns gates near an 11.6-ns theoretical speed limit and intrinsic errors of 2×10⁻⁵, with dephasing models calibrated against published measurements.
watch_item: The reported intrinsic error is not the total error under decoherence, and device-level experimental validation is not described in the abstract.
paper_title: High-fidelity and robust controlled-Z gates for superconducting transmon qubits. I. Intrinsic errors and decoherence
